title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, upgrade actions, and improve run-time caching
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Consolidated and split CI workflows: separate lint, test, and release pipelines; upgraded GitHub Actions and Node matrix; improved caching to reduce build times. No user-facing changes.
description:
Motivation: our monolithic CI workflow has grown slow and brittle as we added more checks (lint, typecheck, unit/e2e tests, and release automation). This PR splits the monorepo CI into targeted workflows, upgrades a set of Actions to current stable versions, and improves cache key hygiene to lower runtime for incremental runs.

What changed (summary):
- Introduced three primary workflows under .github/workflows: lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml. Each workflow is focused and triggers on the appropriate events (PRs, push to main, tags).
- Moved long-running e2e tests to a nightly workflow with an opt-in PR label to keep PR feedback fast.
- Upgraded GitHub Actions/checkout and setup-node actions to the latest stable major versions to support Node 20 matrix and improved caching.
- Normalized caching keys across yarn/npm layers and CI toolchains; added restore/fallback keys for self-hosted runners.
- Extracted common steps into .github/actions/ci-helpers (small scripts) and a lightweight setup-node wrapper to centralize telemetry and node resolution.
- Updated CI docs (docs/ci.md) and added a migration checklist for opensource contributors.

Checklist: [x] split workflows into focused files; [x] update action versions; [x] add cache key improvements; [x] docs updated; [x] run full CI in branch and fix flakes.

Testing notes: I ran multiple PRs from this branch to validate job triggers and cache hits; observed ~30-45% improvement in typical PR runtime for lint+unit test path. Nightly e2e run is unchanged functionally but now isolated so failures don't block PRs.

Related: ENG-4123 (CI performance), ENG-4180 (release automation stability).
